title: Hermes Bots companion plugin contract
description: What the Windows and Android apps exchange with the hermes-bots plugin. Both apps generate their types from this file.

Info.description: Response of GET /api/plugins/hermes-bots/info: the plugin code the dashboard is running.

store_schema.description: Version of the shared store layout

store_id.description: Random id of the shared store, set when the store file is created. A value different from the one a client saw before means the store was recreated and its alert ids restarted: the client reconnects with ?since=0

latest_alert_id.description: Highest alert id issued so far

AlertKind.description: approval and question: a person is asked. resolved: that request was answered, denied or timed out (ref matches the request). finished: a long reply completed. error: a reply failed. routine: routine output was written into the chat. routine_failed: a routine reported a failure, or its output could not be written.

Alert.description: One message on the /api/plugins/hermes-bots/alerts WebSocket. Carries no conversation text.

id.description: Increasing id within one store; reconnect with ?since=<id>. A ?since= above the newest id makes the stream replay every alert the store still keeps, oldest first

session_id.description: Stored session id of the bot's app chat (AppChatRecord). Hook alerts are raised only for that chat, including its continuations after compression and its subagents' sessions, always under the chat's stored id; routine alerts name the chat their target named

ref.description: Request id for approval, question and resolved; turn id for finished and error; null otherwise

Ping.description: Sent on a quiet alert stream every 20 seconds, and at once when the store is recreated during the stream. A store_id different from the one the client holds means the store was recreated: the client resets its last-seen alert id to 0 and keeps reading, because the stream follows this ping with the new store's alerts from the start. Reconnecting would receive them twice.

latest_alert_id.description: The last alert id sent on this stream; 0 in the ping that announces a recreated store

store_id.description: The store's id, as in Info.store_id

AppChatRecord.description: What an app writes into a bot's profile right after creating the bot's chat with session.create. Procedure: read ui_meta and ui_meta_revisions from profiles.list; if ui_meta["hermes-bots-app"] names a chat, use it; otherwise write profiles.configure {name: <bot>, ui_meta: {"hermes-bots-app": <this whole object>}, ui_meta_expected_revisions: {"hermes-bots-app": <revision read>}}, and on a conflict read again and use the recorded chat. The write replaces the whole object, so it always carries every field. The plugin reads it from the profile's profile.yaml to raise hook alerts only for this chat. The key is hermes-bots-app, not hermes-bots, which Hermes's own Bot Mode uses for the bot's title.

chat_session_id.description: Stored session id of the bot's app chat

DeliverTarget.description: Cron deliver value that writes a routine's output into a chat: hbapp:session-<stored session id>/<percent-encoded routine name>. Every character outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ is percent-encoded, including / and ,. Routines deliver text only: attachments in the output are not delivered.

RoutineMessage.description: Content of the assistant-role chat row a routine writes: [Routine: <routine name>] on the first line, then the output.
